title: Possibility, risk, and difficulty
summary: Verb-stem endings that say whether something can happen ({得[う]る}), might go wrong ({おそれがある}, {かねない}), is hard to accept ({がたい}), is politely refused ({かねる}), or is simply impossible ({っこない}).

points.title: 〜得[う]る / 〜得[え]ない
points.structure: V-ます stem + 得[う]る（得[え]る）／ 得[え]ない
points.explanation:
{得[う]る} means "to be possible" in the sense of **likelihood**, not personal skill. {起[お]こり得[う]る} = "could happen", {考[かんが]え得[う]る} = "conceivable". The negative {得[え]ない} means "cannot possibly".

The dictionary form can be read {うる} or {える}; {うる} sounds more formal and written. All other forms use {え}: {得[え]ます}, {得[え]ない}, {得[え]た}.

The most frequent word by far is {あり得[う]る} / {あり得[え]ない}. In casual speech, young people use {ありえない！} to mean "No way! / Unbelievable!".

examples.jp: それは十分[じゅうぶん]あり得[う]る話[はなし]だ。
examples.en: That's an entirely plausible story.

examples.jp: 大[おお]きな地震[じしん]は、いつでも起[お]こり得[う]る。
examples.en: A major earthquake could happen at any time.

examples.jp: 考[かんが]え得[う]る限[かぎ]りの方法[ほうほう]を試[ため]した。
examples.en: We tried every method we could think of.

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]は、一社[いっしゃ]だけでは解決[かいけつ]し得[え]ない。
examples.en: This problem cannot be solved by one company alone.

points.notes: Not for ability: ✗ {私[わたし]は泳[およ]ぎ得[う]る}. Use {泳[およ]げる} for "I can swim".

quiz.q: このような事故[じこ]は、どの工場[こうじょう]でも起[お]こり＿＿。
quiz.en: An accident like this could happen at any factory.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]が嘘[うそ]をつくなんて、あり＿＿。
quiz.en: There's no way she would lie.

points.title: 〜おそれがある
points.meaning: there is a risk / danger that
points.structure: V-dictionary + おそれがある　／　Noun + のおそれがある
points.explanation:
{おそれ} (written {恐[おそ]れ} or {虞[おそれ]}) means "fear, danger". {〜おそれがある} warns that something **bad** might happen. It is objective and formal, so it is the standard expression in weather reports, safety warnings, medicine labels and news.

It is never used for good possibilities. For a neutral "might", use {〜かもしれない} or {〜可能性[かのうせい]がある}.

The polite form {〜おそれがあります} is standard in announcements. Earthquake bulletins use a related phrase for the opposite case: {津波[つなみ]の心配[しんぱい]はありません} ("there is no danger of a tsunami").

examples.jp: 台風[たいふう]の影響[えいきょう]で、明日[あした]は大雨[おおあめ]になるおそれがあります。
examples.en: Due to the typhoon, there is a risk of heavy rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: この薬[くすり]は眠[ねむ]くなるおそれがあるので、運転[うんてん]の前[まえ]には飲[の]まないでください。
examples.en: This medicine may cause drowsiness, so do not take it before driving.

examples.jp: 津波[つなみ]のおそれがあるため、海岸[かいがん]から離[はな]れてください。
examples.en: Because of the risk of a tsunami, please move away from the coast.

examples.jp: このままでは、顧客[こきゃく]の情報[じょうほう]が外部[がいぶ]に漏[も]れるおそれがある。
examples.en: If things continue like this, customer information could leak outside the company.

quiz.q: 大雨[おおあめ]により、今夜[こんや]川[かわ]が氾濫[はんらん]する＿＿があります。
quiz.en: Due to the heavy rain, there is a risk the river will flood tonight.

quiz.q: この製品[せいひん]は、使[つか]い方[かた]によっては火災[かさい]につながる＿＿があります。
quiz.en: Depending on how it is used, this product could cause a fire.

points.title: 〜かねない
points.meaning: might well (do something bad); could end up
points.structure: V-ます stem + かねない
points.explanation:
Despite the {ない}, {かねない} is **not** negative in meaning. It says "there's a real chance this bad thing will happen". It reflects the speaker's own worry or criticism, so it is more subjective than {おそれがある}.

Typical uses: warning someone ({事故[じこ]を起[お]こしかねない}), pointing out risks at work ({問題[もんだい]になりかねない}), or saying a person is capable of doing something bad ({あの人[ひと]なら言[い]いかねない}).

It is used in both speech and writing; the polite form is {かねません}.

examples.jp: そんな運転[うんてん]をしていたら、事故[じこ]を起[お]こしかねないよ。
examples.en: If you drive like that, you could well cause an accident.

examples.jp: 睡眠不足[すいみんぶそく]が続[つづ]くと、体[からだ]を壊[こわ]しかねません。
examples.en: If your lack of sleep continues, you may end up ruining your health.

examples.jp: 小[ちい]さなミスが、大[おお]きな問題[もんだい]につながりかねない。
examples.en: A small mistake could lead to a big problem.

examples.jp: あの人[ひと]なら、そのくらいのことは言[い]いかねない。
examples.en: He's just the kind of person who might say something like that.

points.notes: {おそれがある}: objective warning (news, labels). {かねない}: the speaker's own concern. Neither is used for good outcomes.

quiz.q: このままでは、締[し]め切[き]りに間[ま]に合[あ]わなくなり＿＿。
quiz.en: At this rate, we could end up missing the deadline.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]の不用意[ふようい]な発言[はつげん]は、誤解[ごかい]を招[まね]き＿＿。
quiz.en: His careless remark could well cause misunderstandings.

points.title: 〜かねる
points.meaning: cannot (politely); be unable to bring oneself to
points.structure: V-ます stem + かねる / かねます
points.explanation:
{かねる} means "I find it hard to / I'm not in a position to". In practice it is a **polite refusal**, and it is everywhere in Japanese customer service and business:
- {わかりかねます} "I'm afraid I can't say"
- {お答[こた]えしかねます} "I'm unable to answer"
- {いたしかねます} "We are unable to do that"

It sounds softer than {できません} because it suggests the speaker would like to help but can't. Outside of business it can express personal reluctance: {賛成[さんせい]しかねる} ("I can't quite agree").

Don't confuse it with {かねない} ("might well"), which looks negative but isn't.

examples.jp: 申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございませんが、そのご質問[しつもん]にはお答[こた]えしかねます。
examples.en: I'm very sorry, but I'm unable to answer that question.

examples.jp: 個人情報[こじんじょうほう]に関[かん]することは、お教[おし]えいたしかねます。
examples.en: We are unable to disclose anything relating to personal information.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]の一存[いちぞん]では決[き]めかねますので、上司[じょうし]に確認[かくにん]いたします。
examples.en: I can't decide that on my own, so I'll check with my manager.

examples.jp: 正直[しょうじき]に言[い]うと、彼[かれ]の意見[いけん]には賛成[さんせい]しかねる。
examples.en: To be honest, I can't quite agree with his opinion.

examples.jp: 困[こま]っている様子[ようす]を見[み]るに見[み]かねて、手伝[てつだ]うことにした。
examples.en: I couldn't bear to just stand by and watch them struggle, so I decided to help.

points.notes: Remember: {かねる} = can't (polite refusal); {かねない} = might (bad thing). The idiom {見[み]るに見[み]かねて} means "unable to stand by and watch".

quiz.q: 申[もう]し訳[わけ]ございませんが、返品[へんぴん]はお受[う]けいたし＿＿。
quiz.en: We're very sorry, but we are unable to accept returns.

quiz.q: その件[けん]については、私[わたし]には判断[はんだん]し＿＿ので、担当者[たんとうしゃ]におつなぎします。
quiz.en: I'm not able to make a judgment on that matter, so I'll put you through to the person in charge.

points.title: 〜がたい
points.explanation:
{がたい} (from {難[かた]い}, "difficult") means that something is hard to do because of **inner resistance**: you can't bring yourself to believe it, forgive it or forget it. Common combinations: {信[しん]じがたい}, {許[ゆる]しがたい}, {理解[りかい]しがたい}, {忘[わす]れがたい}, {耐[た]えがたい}, {得[え]がたい} (precious, hard to come by).

It is formal and somewhat literary. You will see it in news commentary, essays and speeches.

For **physical or practical** difficulty, use {〜にくい} instead: {この靴[くつ]は歩[ある]きにくい}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]がそんなことをしたとは、信[しん]じがたい。
examples.en: It's hard to believe that he did such a thing.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもを狙[ねら]った犯罪[はんざい]は、許[ゆる]しがたい。
examples.en: Crimes targeting children are unforgivable.

examples.jp: 留学中[りゅうがくちゅう]の一年[いちねん]は、忘[わす]れがたい思[おも]い出[で]になった。
examples.en: My year studying abroad became an unforgettable memory.

examples.jp: あのチームで働[はたら]けたことは、得[え]がたい経験[けいけん]だった。
examples.en: Being able to work on that team was an invaluable experience.

points.notes: {にくい} = hard for practical reasons (the pen is hard to write with). {がたい} = hard to accept emotionally or morally. {ありがたい} ("grateful") originally meant "rare, hard to exist".

quiz.q: 毎日[まいにち]一緒[いっしょ]に働[はたら]いていた彼[かれ]が会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を盗[ぬす]んだなんて、信[しん]じ＿＿。
quiz.en: It's hard to believe that he, who worked with us every day, stole company money.

quiz.q: この靴[くつ]は重[おも]くて歩[ある]き＿＿。
quiz.en: These shoes are heavy and hard to walk in.

points.title: 〜っこない
points.meaning: no way; there's no chance that
points.structure: V-ます stem + っこない
points.explanation:
{っこない} is a strong, casual denial: "there's no way that will happen". Common combinations are {できっこない}, {わかりっこない}, {勝[か]てっこない}, {間[ま]に合[あ]いっこない}, {ばれっこない}.

It is **spoken and informal**, used with friends and family. In writing or polite speech, use {〜はずがない}, {〜わけがない} or {〜得[え]ない} instead.

It attaches to the verb stem, so it is {わかりっこない}, not ✗ {わからっこない}.

examples.jp: こんな難[むずか]しい問題[もんだい]、子[こ]どもにわかりっこないよ。
examples.en: There's no way a kid could understand a problem this hard.

examples.jp: 一日[いちにち]で全部[ぜんぶ]覚[おぼ]えるなんて、できっこない。
examples.en: Memorising all of it in one day? No way.

examples.jp: 黙[だま]っていれば、ばれっこないよ。
examples.en: If you keep quiet, there's no way anyone will find out.

examples.jp: あのチームに勝[か]てっこないってみんな言[い]うけど、やってみなきゃわからない。
examples.en: Everyone says there's no way we can beat that team, but you never know until you try.

quiz.q: 宝[たから]くじなんて、当[あ]たり＿＿よ。
quiz.en: There's no way you'll win the lottery.

quiz.q: 三十分[さんじゅっぷん]でレポートを書[か]くなんて、＿＿。
quiz.en: Write a report in thirty minutes? There's no way I can do that.
